evidence.observation: 11 callable symbols cover setup, request construction, delivery field checks, snapshots, and the auto-created delivery row. The helper supplies DeliveryFeePiastres=1000 and DeliveryServiceId=svc-1; initialization seeds user/product/open shift and does not seed a DeliveryService. It asserts persistence of client-supplied fee/name/id, but does not challenge service existence/activity/fee authority.

Checkout wraps request.DeliveryFeePiastres directly as Money; for delivery it only validates non-empty service ID through DeliveryRules and composes address; it prices with that fee and snapshots request service ID/name. No service entity lookup/Active check/fee resolution in the examined flow.
Payable total includes caller-provided deliveryFee; negative result clamps to zero, with no fee validation in this rule.
Request carries DeliveryFeePiastres and free-form service ID/name.
Catalog exposes active service IDs, names, and fees to delivery-facing clients; separate all-services management query exists.

Delivery managers create/update catalog fee and active flag; handler comments say historical orders snapshot service id/name/fee at checkout, supporting (but not conclusively proving) catalog-authoritative intent.
UI documentation says selection reuses backend delivery services list rather than client fee guesses; viewmodel holds selected service DTO.
Normal UI sends selected service DTO fee/id/name in checkout request.

bounded_assessment.mechanics: SOURCE_CONFIRMED: the authenticated checkout path accepts caller-supplied delivery fee and service snapshot instead of resolving an active catalog service and current fee.
bounded_assessment.condition: The integrity impact depends on the intended pricing authority. Normal UI follows the backend active-service list; an API caller with checkout authorization can send a different fee or unrelated/inactive service ID/name.
bounded_assessment.effect: If catalog price is authoritative, a caller can lower the collected payable total (including to zero with sufficiently negative fee because ComputePayableTotal clamps) or overstate it; the persisted order snapshot can disagree with catalog. No runtime occurrence or policy-approved override was established.
bounded_assessment.counterevidence: Normal UI selects a backend-returned service fee; delivery service maintenance is permission-gated and the service update comment describes checkout-time snapshots. These establish a clear intended catalog workflow, while leaving authority/override policy unstated. No matching issue text was found in financial-findings.json.The test class XML comment at lines 8-15 says the Cashier app has no delivery order-type UI; the current WinUI Delivery viewmodel and Checkout viewmodel provide that path, so that part of the test comment is stale. This does not change the source-confirmed request fee trust gap.
bounded_assessment.tests: The test fixture supplies svc-1 and fee 1000 without a DeliveryService seed and expects them persisted; it therefore exercises required-field validation and snapshot behavior, not catalog binding. No tested inactive, unknown-service, or tampered-fee case identified.
bounded_assessment.classification: CONDITIONAL_STATIC_SOURCE_GAP; resolve against intended pricing policy before promoting to confirmed financial finding. Static-only; no runtime or database tests executed.
bounded_assessment.recommendation: If active catalog fees are authoritative, resolve service ID server-side, require active status, use its fee/name, and add integration cases for unknown/inactive service and a tampered fee. If negotiated overrides are intended, specify and authorize/audit them explicitly.
